problem: Point-goal navigation methods that rely on depth do so via a depth sensor or ground-truth depth supervision, and degrade sharply for RGB-only agents. Off-the-shelf self-supervised monocular depth suffers scale ambiguity, and simple late fusion (addition) of RGB and depth features is weak.
motivation: Scene geometry (e.g. obstacle avoidance) is critical for efficient navigation, but realistic monocular agents have no GT depth. Learning scale-consistent depth from the agent's own consecutive frames and fusing it well with RGB could give an RGB-only agent both better performance and better training efficiency.
key_idea: Geo-Nav learns scale-consistent depth from a monocular RGB camera with a self-supervised network (SDE, with bidirectional geometry-consistency loss) and fuses RGB and depth features with patch-wise cross-modality attention at multiple scales (CPF) before a standard LSTM PPO policy.
insight: Scale consistency is essential: removing the geometry-consistency loss L_GC drops depth AbsRel quality from 0.134 to 3.195 and navigation SPL from 84.7 to 68.9. Once depth quality is acceptable, its source barely matters (GT depth 85.2 SPL, supervised depth 84.6, self-supervised 84.7). Cross-modality attention gives most of the fusion gain (w/o CA 81.5 vs full 84.7 SPL), and SDE-pretrained encoders beat ImageNet weights (78.2 vs 84.7).
method: Self-supervised Depth Estimation (SDE): depth net + pose net trained on pure-translation image pairs from agent trajectories with photometric (L1+SSIM), edge-aware smoothness and bidirectional geometry-consistency losses (weights 1/0.1/0.5)
Training data for SDE: 1K triplets per Gibson scene, 180K triplets in total, agent step size 0.05m to keep frames similar

Cross-modality Attention (CA): 16x16 patch tokens with learnable shared positional embedding; depth tokens as query, RGB tokens as key/value; multi-head attention plus FFN, skip connection and layer norm

Multi-scale Fusion (MSF): CA applied at four stages (strides 2,4,8,16) of RGB (ResNet18, initialised from the SDE encoder) and depth encoders; fused features fed to the next stage; reshape layer restores 2D shape
Policy network: LSTM with policy and value heads; input is concatenation of fused visual features, previous action embedding, goal direction embedding and hidden state

Training: freeze SDE and visual encoders; imitation-learning warm-up (10M steps, lr 2.5e-4), then PPO fine-tuning (lr 1e-4, reward = geodesic distance delta + success bonus + time penalty), 100M steps total

setting.backbone: ResNet18 RGB encoder + depth encoder (SDE) + cross-modality attention + LSTM PPO policy (trained from scratch, visual encoders frozen during policy training)
setting.training_data: Gibson train (72 scenes, 5M episodes) for IL+PPO with 100M steps; SDE trained on 180K self-collected image triplets from Gibson; no GT depth
setting.observation: monocular RGB (256x256) + relative goal direction/distance (GPS+compass style point-goal)
setting.action_space: low-level: MoveForward 0.25 m, TurnLeft 10°, TurnRight 10°, Stop
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT-depth variant is only an ablation); noise-free point-goal indication; SDE data collected with simulator-provided rollouts

numbers.backbone: ResNet18 RGB + SDE depth + CPF + LSTM
numbers.extra: trained on Gibson only, 100M steps, 1 V100 for 7 days; RGB-only (no depth sensor); 500-step budget, 0.2 m success radius

numbers_note: Val on 994 episodes in 14 unseen Gibson environments; reported as mean±std, means copied. Geo-Nav w/ IDM auxiliary reaches SPL 85.7 / Success 95 (text only).
results: On Gibson PointNav, RGB-only Geo-Nav achieves SPL 84.7 / SR 93.5, beating DD-PPO trained on Gibson only for 100M steps (79.2/92.1), Mid-Level (78.9/91.7) and a ResNet18 DD-PPO variant (82.7/89.6). It reaches similar SPL to DD-PPO (83.6 vs 82.5) with 4 vs 27 GPU-days, i.e. ~6x faster training.
limitations: Only evaluated in simulation on Gibson with noise-free point-goal indications; no real-robot or other benchmarks
Multi-stage pipeline (SDE pretraining, IL warm-up, PPO) and frozen encoders; depth estimator trained on in-domain Gibson data may not generalise to other scenes
